To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the propagation of interlaminar delamination, mode transition, sublaminate buckle propagation, matrix and fiber cracking and the interactions of these mechanisms govern the failure of composites upon compression loading after an impact event.

the failure mechanism upon compression after impact in woven fiber composites involves delamination and sublaminate bucking, followed by the initiation and propagation of matrix microcracking, fiber cracking and fiber kinking.
compression-after-impact damage propagation is governed by the propagation of delamination followed by sublaminate bucking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the compression-after-impact response in composite materials and structures.
the compression-after-impact response in woven fiber-reinfoced composites and provides a comprehensive understanding of the compression failure mechanisms in these materials.
the development of a reduced order multiscales model that can be utilized to predict the compression-after-impact behavior of woven fiber-reinfoced composites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the compression-after-impact (CAI) failure of a composite laminate is due to the interaction of the impact-induced damage mechanisms with the applied compressive load, leading to a shear failure of the composite.
the impact event initiates a sequence of failure mechanisms, which are responsible for the ultimate failure of the structure.
the compression failure is due to extensive delamination, which is preceded by a mode transition and sublaminate buckle propagation, and is followed by matrix cracking and fiber fracture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in addition to the sublaminate delamination and buckling, the constituent damage plays a critical role in determining the compression failure of the impacted composite structure.
compression-after-impact behavior of woven composites can be understood by considering the interactions of the constituent microcracking with delamination.
the propagation of impact induced delamination is the primary cause of ultimate compression-after-impact (CAI) failure of woven fiber-reinfoced composites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
compression failure of composite structures is due to a sequence of damage mechanisms.
compression-after-impact response is governed by a complex interaction of damage mechanisms, and the failure is preceded by extensive propagation of delaminations and sublaminate bucklings.
the compression-after-impact response is a function of the initial damage state and the material system.
